To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

physical activity and cognitive exercises, in association with other medical therapies might lead to significant ameliorations of symptoms in chronic diseases, and that sirtuins are involved in these beneficial outcomes.

physical and cognitive exercises activate the expression of Sirt1, Sirt2, Sirt3 and Sirt6 in different tissues and cell types, and this activation might be associated with beneficial or harmful effects in the pathophysiology of chronic diseases.

(1) Sirt1 is involved in the regulation of mitochondrial dynamics, (2) Sirt1 and Sirt3 are involved in the regulation and expression of genes involved in the control of mitochondrial function and (3) Sirt1 regulates the expression of genes involved with mitochondrial biogenesis and metabolism.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the molecular mechanisms of the positive effects of exercise in chronic pathophysiological conditions.
the study of the molecular mechanisms of the beneficial effects of physical exercise on the elderly and on the identification of novel targets to improve the quality of their life.
the identification of new epigenetic therapeutic targets for the treatment of chronic diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Sirtuins play a pivotal role in the pathophysiology of chronic diseases.
sirtuins are a promising target to be explored in rehabilitation medicine and that their role in chronic diseases needs to be further investigated.
sirtuins are involved in the pathophysiological conditions of the elderly, but the final outcome of their action is often difficult to establish.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the role of Sirt in chronic non-transmittable diseases is controversial, and that the effect is dependent on the type of exercise, the type of chronic non-transmissible disease, and the age of the patient.
sirtuins might play a positive or negative role in aging and age-related diseases depending on the tissue, the disease, the stage of the disease and the type and intensity of the physical activity.

Sirts are a family of NAD-dependent deacetylases and ADP-ribosyltransferases that are involved in the modulation of a variety of biological processes, including metabolism, stress response, and aging.
The main takeaway from our work is that
sirtuins might be a promising tool for the design of innovative therapeutic strategies in chronic diseases.
Sirts, as well as their modulators, represent a novel class of potential pharmacological and nutritional targets to be exploited in the treatment of non-transmissible chronic diseases.
sirtuins might represent a new therapeutic target in the field of rehabilitation medicine.
